classification.difficultyReason: Recognise the rectangle's diagonal as the circle's diameter, find it using Pythagoras' theorem, then calculate the circle's area.

content.prompt: In the diagram to the right, $ABCD$ is a rectangle in which $AB=8\text{ cm}$ and $BC=6\text{ cm}$. Find the area of the circle in $\text{cm}^2$.

spec.description: Unshaded circle through all four vertices of an axis-aligned rectangle. A is bottom-left, B bottom-right, C top-right and D top-left. The 8 cm label is inside above AB; the 6 cm label is inside beside BC. Ordinary source blue outlines become house black. No centre, diagonal or radius is supplied.
spec.mathematics: Rectangle vertices (-4,-3), (4,-3), (4,3), (-4,3) lie on the circle x squared plus y squared equals 25; horizontal sides have length 8 and vertical sides have length 6.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the original rectangle, circle, vertex labels and given side lengths are visible.

answer.short:
$25\pi\text{ cm}^2$

The rectangle's diagonal is the circle's diameter.
answer.worked:
The rectangle's diagonals bisect each other at the circle's centre, so diagonal $AC$ is a diameter. By Pythagoras' theorem in right-angled triangle $ABC$:

$$\begin{align*}AC^2&=8^2+6^2\\AC^2&=100\\AC&=10\text{ cm}\\r&=\frac{10}{2}\\r&=5\text{ cm}\\A&=\pi r^2\\A&=\pi\times5^2\\A&=25\pi\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
